html:
SMTO-ART-0025 — SMTO needs you to be signed in to open this file

GUID: 7adb07c3-79f1-437c-99d0-a86d80a59c47
Slug: artifact-authentication-required
Domain: ART · Subsystem: art

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't confirm who was asking for this Task file, so it didn't open it. This usually happens after your sign-in expires or when a file link is opened in another browser. The file itself is unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Reload the SMTO page in your browser. If the Sign in page appears, sign in again. File access from a page lasts up to 12 hours and ends when your sign-in does, so signing in gives the page fresh access.
  2. Open the conversation and open the file from Artifacts from this run, instead of using a saved or copied file link. Opening it from that list lets SMTO renew the page's file access automatically before loading the file.
  3. Use the same browser where you're signed in to SMTO. A link pasted into another browser, a private window, or another device carries no sign-in. SMTO ties file access to the browser you signed in with, so any other browser is treated as unknown.

What success looks like

  • The file preview or download starts, and Artifacts from this run lists your files.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't paste your password or any access key into a Task, a screenshot, or the error report.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The artifact API found no signed-in portal account, no valid AOR_ARTIFACT_API_TOKEN credential and no unexpired of_artifact_session cookie, so it returned an authentication challenge.

What this means

  • Artifact access checks find no session/API token or cannot validate the supplied token. Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.

Why this can happen

  • Artifact access checks find no session/API token or cannot validate the supplied token.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect the owning authenticated conversation/session or supported API credential, without copying tokens into URLs or prompts.

How to fix it

  • Browser clients must reach /api/agent/artifacts* through the signed-in SMTO portal; the UI renews the 12-hour of_artifact_session cookie through POST /api/agent/artifact-session once after a 401. Scripts must send AOR_ARTIFACT_API_TOKEN as a Bearer token or Basic password; never place that token in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostics.
  • Open the artifact from its authenticated owning conversation or use the supported authenticated API.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended client authenticates through the supported artifact access flow.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Artifact publication and presentation remain separate from the command that produced a file. Only an explicit pre-dispatch rejection proves that new command did not run; diagnostics do not collect, transfer, quarantine or delete files.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
